market.headline: Hotter producer prices put Fed rate-hike talk back on the table and hit chip stocks (QQQ -1.2%, SPY -0.4%). Nvidia's first report without Jensen Huang, due around Nov 17, is the next big test.
market.day_type: Rate scare plus chip selloff. The October inflation data and Fed comments pushed yields higher, and Nvidia's leadership crisis and fears of tighter China rules hit AI hardware. Buyers moved into cheaper big tech instead: META, AAPL and MSFT finished up.
watch: Monday open: QQQ closed at 679.89, just under its 200-day average of 681.20, and traded at 674.60 after hours. A break below Friday's low of 671.71 means more chip selling.
SPY: Friday's low of 747.89 is the line, and it traded at 750.06 after hours. Below it, the 200-day average at 729.32 comes into view.
Nvidia earnings around Nov 17 (date not confirmed) set the tone for AMD, AVGO, MU, TSM, ARM, SMCI and CRWV.

stocks.headline: Down 2.0% to 162.85 on 1.8x normal volume. It is down 23.9% in 20 days and 33.1% below its 52-week high. Morning call: right, because the 166.19 hold never happened and no buy triggered.
stocks.why: The business is the strongest on this list: sales are up 106%, the operating margin is 65%, and forecasts are up 24% in 90 days. Yet the stock trades at only 10x next year's profit. The selling is about people and politics. Huang has resigned. Washington has a spy probe and a feud between Treasury and Commerce. Tighter China chip rules are feared. Melius and Craig-Hallum cut it to Hold, at targets of 185 and 180. The real damage the news can do is to China sales and to the AI-financing chain that funds buyers like CRWV. A weak outlook next week would drag every chip name here down with it.

long_term.reason: This matches the house view. The profits are real and cheap, but the company has no permanent CEO and China policy is unsettled. That is too much unknown to add before the report.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A credible permanent CEO plus a strong outlook at the report makes it Add on dips. New China sales bans make it Trim.
stocks.action: Don't buy before the report. Owners hold unless it closes below 148.80.

levels.means: above = buyers are back after the CEO shock; below = the bounce is still being sold
above = Friday's floor holds; below = a retest of the low is likely
above = the 52-week low holds; below = owners cut the position

stocks.headline: Down 8.8% to 534.06 on 1.5x normal volume, the worst drop on the list, with no company news. Morning call: right, because it did not hold 554.90 and no buy triggered.
stocks.why: This was profit-taking, not a business problem. The stock was up 18.9% in five days and 21% since its report, and with a beta of 2.00 it falls hardest when rates and Nvidia fears hit chips. The numbers are still good. Sales are up 45% and speeding up, the operating margin doubled to 18% from 9%, and forecasts are up 15% in 90 days. BofA raised its target to 700 on Thursday. The weak spot is price: 126x last year's profit against 38x for peers. That leaves room for more giveback if Nvidia disappoints.

long_term.reason: This matches the house view. Growth is strong, but at this price it falls twice as hard as the market whenever chips sell off.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A close back above 554.90 after a solid Nvidia report turns it into Add on dips.
stocks.action: Don't buy Monday. Owners hold while it stays above 519.02, and new money waits for a close above 554.90.

levels.means: above = the selloff is over and buying can resume; below = old support has turned into a ceiling
above = the 20-day uptrend is intact; below = owners trim, since more giveback toward the 402.10 area of the 20-day range is likely

stocks.headline: Down 6.1% to 53.13. It gave back part of the 24.7% jump after its Nov 10 report. Morning call: right, because 58.56 was never reached.
stocks.why: CRWV is the stock most exposed to the AI-financing worry that Huang's exit set off. Its backlog is huge at $132.3B and sales are up 168%. But it still loses money: $1.27 a share last quarter and a -1% operating margin. It carries $24.9B of long-term debt against $4.1B of cash. Higher rates make that debt costlier, and any pullback by Nvidia or lenders hits it first. If Nvidia's report goes well, it bounces hardest. If not, it falls hardest.

long_term.reason: This matches the house swing view of Avoid. The growth rests on borrowed money while rates are rising and its main supplier is in crisis.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A quarter with positive operating profit, or a clear funding deal that lowers its debt risk.
stocks.action: Don't buy Monday. Look again only after a close above 58.56.

levels.means: above = buyers have taken back the post-earnings high; below = the post-earnings pop is fading
above = Friday's low holds; below = it heads back toward the 40.58 52-week low
